added: Windows: new POST /clear-avatars route and matching queue command. NewProject() clears garments only - the SDK header states this explicitly (UtilityAPIInterface.h:419-421, 'Clear the current garment and begin a new garment') and avatars demonstrably survive it. Avatars therefore accumulated across pipeline runs in a single CLO session, and step_11 was extracting the wrong one, exporting a base or previous-user body under the current run's id. This route calls UTILITY_API->DeleteAvatar() to remove them. Accepts optional {"max_index": N}; currently informational only since the delete list is driven by the plugin's own counter (see below).

Windows: g_avatarsLoaded atomic counter. The plugin now tracks how many avatars it imported instead of asking CLO, because every per-index avatar query API available is unsafe (see known_issues). Incremented on successful import-avatar-avt, reset to 0 only when DeleteAvatar succeeds. Deliberately NOT reset by new-project: avatars survive NewProject, so zeroing it there would make the following clear-avatars delete nothing and leak exactly what it exists to remove.

Windows: per-call TraceLog BEGIN/END instrumentation inside clear-avatars. Doc 09 section 6.2 argued this was the highest-value instrumentation available; it proved itself on the first live test by naming the exact crashing call in a single run.
changed: Windows: import-avatar-avt now increments g_avatarsLoaded on success and logs the running total in its END trace line.
fixed: Windows: avatars leaking between pipeline runs in one CLO session. Root cause confirmed by reading saved projects directly - passing runs contained exactly one .avt member in result_project.zprj, failing runs contained two or three, and the correct avatar was present every time but was not the one extracted. See .agent/website-launch-2/11-date-26_08_22.md Part 2 for the full evidence.
known_issues: UTILITY_API->GetAvatarProperties(index) CRASHES the CLO process outright when no avatar exists at that index. Confirmed live 2026-08-22: a bare /clear-avatars against an empty scene logged 'probe GetAvatarProperties(0) begin' with no matching end, and the CLO process was gone. This is despite GetAvatarProperties living in UtilityAPIInterface rather than the SEH-crash-prone EXPORT_API family. Do not use it, or any other per-index avatar query, to determine what exists.

There is consequently NO safe way to ask CLO how many avatars are in the scene. GetAvatarCount and GetAvatarNameList are in EXPORT_API (already excluded per POST_MORTEM_v1.1.1.md), GetAvatarProperties crashes as above, and IsShowAvatar cannot distinguish 'hidden' from 'absent' since its default body returns false for both. The g_avatarsLoaded counter exists because of this.

UTILITY_API->DeleteAvatar() HANGS CLO's main thread when the index list contains an index with no avatar at it. Confirmed live 2026-08-22: 'BEGIN clear-avatars tracked=2' then 'DeleteAvatar begin count=2' with no matching end, against a scene holding only one avatar. Recovery requires killing and relaunching CLO. Both deleting and querying an absent index are therefore unsafe.

/clear-avatars is consequently NOT CALLED by the pipeline. The route and the g_avatarsLoaded counter remain in the plugin but are dead code as of 2026-08-22 - step_07 no longer invokes them. Do not re-enable without first solving how to learn, safely, how many avatars the scene holds. Every known approach is ruled out: GetAvatarCount/GetAvatarNameList (EXPORT_API, SEH-crash-prone), GetAvatarProperties (crashes on absent index), IsShowAvatar (cannot distinguish hidden from absent), and counting our own imports (wrong - the pipeline imports twice per run but the scene often ends with one avatar, so the patched import replaces rather than adds).

g_avatarsLoaded only tracks avatars imported through this plugin. An avatar loaded by hand through the CLO GUI is invisible to it, so clear-avatars will not remove that one. Acceptable for the automated pipeline; this is not a general-purpose scene cleaner.
Carried over from v1.3.1 and still open: POST /export hangs indefinitely against a completely empty CLO scene. Not a blocker - the real pipeline always loads an avatar first.
Carried over: Mac not ported. Windows-only focus.

notes: Built against CLO_SDK_v2026.0.356_WIN (SDK v10.0.3), matching the Qt 6.10 migration the vendor changelog requires a rebuild for. The preceding 2025.2.368-built plugin hung CLO permanently on NewProject() after the app was upgraded to 2026.1.188 on 2026-08-15 - see .agent/website-launch-2/09-windows-plugin-commit-audit-new-project-hang.md and new-project-bug-writeup-26_8_9.md section 9. This version pairs with Python-side changes in step_11_save_outputs.py, which now selects the highest-numbered .avt member from the saved project rather than the first, and hard-fails any run whose saved project contains other than exactly one avatar - so a leak is reported rather than silently corrected. Needs rebuild + manual install (Administrator) + CLO restart before use.
